directAnswer: To test a subnet mask, you can use the command line to ping an IP address within the subnet and check connectivity. Alternatively, you can use network tools to verify the subnet configuration.
summary: Testing a subnet mask involves checking connectivity and verifying configuration using command line tools or network utilities.

sections.heading: Understanding Subnet Masks
sections.body: A subnet mask defines the network and host portions of an IP address. Understanding how it works is crucial for testing.

sections.heading: Using Command Line Tools
sections.body: You can use tools like 'ping' and 'ipconfig' or 'ifconfig' to test connectivity and view current subnet configurations.

sections.heading: Network Utilities
sections.body: There are various network utilities available that can help visualize and test subnet configurations, such as Angry IP Scanner and Advanced IP Scanner.

steps.title: Open Command Line
steps.detail: Access the command line interface on your device (Command Prompt on Windows, Terminal on macOS/Linux).

steps.title: Check IP Configuration
steps.detail: Run 'ipconfig' (Windows) or 'ifconfig' (macOS/Linux) to view your current IP address and subnet mask.

steps.title: Ping an IP Address
steps.detail: Use the 'ping' command followed by an IP address within the same subnet to test connectivity (e.g., 'ping 192.168.1.1').

steps.title: Use Network Utility
steps.detail: Download and run a network utility tool to scan the subnet and verify active devices.

faqs.question: What is a subnet mask?
faqs.answer: A subnet mask is a 32-bit number that divides an IP address into the network and host portions.

faqs.question: How can I find my subnet mask?
faqs.answer: You can find your subnet mask by running 'ipconfig' on Windows or 'ifconfig' on macOS/Linux.

faqs.question: What does it mean if I can't ping an IP address in my subnet?
faqs.answer: If you can't ping an IP address in your subnet, it may indicate a configuration issue, firewall settings, or that the device is offline.

caveats: Ensure that your firewall settings allow ICMP packets for ping tests.
Subnet configurations may vary based on network architecture and device settings.
